# @mono-agent/agent-orchestrator

Use this package to let one orchestrator delegate bounded subtasks to named
structural responders through a request-scoped MCP tool.

## Responsibility

Reusable orchestration helpers for exposing named collaborator responders to an orchestrator runtime. The first surface is an MCP tool named `AskCollaborator`, bound to loopback by default, that lets the orchestrator model decide which collaborator to ask, and how many times, before producing its final answer.

This is a **plugin-tier** package: it publishes to npm in the mono-agent lockstep at the same version as the core packages, but it is not part of the core `@mono-agent/agent-app` dependency closure. Hosts consume it directly as a request-scoped runtime extension — it is not a `channels.plugins[]` channel.

## Install / Usage

```bash
pnpm add @mono-agent/agent-orchestrator@latest @mono-agent/agent-app@latest @mono-agent/config@latest
```

<!-- doc-test:typescript -->

```ts
import { createConfiguredAgentResponder } from "@mono-agent/agent-app";
import type { MonoAgentConfig } from "@mono-agent/config";
import {
  createCollaboratorToolRuntimeExtension,
  type OrchestratorCollaborator,
} from "@mono-agent/agent-orchestrator";

export async function createOrchestrator(
  config: MonoAgentConfig,
  collaborators: readonly OrchestratorCollaborator[],
) {
  return createConfiguredAgentResponder({
    config,
    runtimeOptionsForRequest: async ({ request }) => {
      const extension = await createCollaboratorToolRuntimeExtension({
        collaborators,
        conversationId: request.conversationId,
        originalUserMessage: request.userMessage,
        abortSignal: request.abortSignal,
      });
      return {
        runtimeOptions: extension.runtimeOptions,
        cleanup: extension.cleanup,
      };
    },
  });
}
```

Hosts create one request-scoped extension, merge `extension.runtimeOptions` into the orchestrator runtime call, and call `extension.cleanup()` after the request. Collaborators are plain `AgentResponder` instances, so hosts can wrap local agents, A2A consumers, or other adapter-owned responders without this package depending on those adapters.

The default host is `127.0.0.1`. A non-loopback `host` is rejected unless the
caller also sets `allowNonLoopback: true`. That explicit opt-in exposes an MCP
endpoint with no package-owned bearer authentication, so use it only behind a
trusted network or an authentication boundary you control.

Keep every installed `@mono-agent/*` package on the same lockstep version.
Older standalone `0.4.0` installs pulled retired settings dependencies and should
be upgraded as a set.

## Architecture

The extension creates a bounded MCP boundary for one orchestrator request:

### Data flow

1. The host supplies named `AgentResponder` collaborators and the parent
   request's conversation id, message, and abort signal.
2. The extension starts a loopback-by-default Streamable HTTP MCP server on an
   ephemeral port by default and exposes one `AskCollaborator` tool. A caller
   may select a fixed port; non-loopback binding requires the explicit
   `allowNonLoopback` opt-in described above.
3. Each tool call validates the collaborator id and global call cap, derives a
   collaborator-specific conversation id, and invokes that responder.
4. Collaborator text becomes the tool result; failures, timeouts, and unknown
   ids become visible MCP tool errors for the orchestrator model.
5. The host calls the idempotent `cleanup()` after the runtime and its tool
   clients settle.

### Package structure

The implementation is intentionally one source module: `src/index.ts` owns
option validation, safe binding, MCP request handling, abort/timeout composition,
responder dispatch, result normalization, and cleanup.

## Public API

### Start here

| API | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `createCollaboratorToolRuntimeExtension()` | Create one request-scoped MCP server and the runtime options that expose it |
| `OrchestratorCollaborator` | Name and describe a structural responder, with an optional per-call timeout |
| `CollaboratorToolRuntimeExtension` | Read the bound URL/options and close the server through idempotent `cleanup()` |
| `DEFAULT_COLLABORATOR_MAX_CALLS` | Inspect the default six-call request budget |

## Dependency Boundary

This package may depend on core agent contracts and the MCP TypeScript SDK. It must not depend on communication adapters, the agent harness, operator surfaces, host demos, or concrete runtime packages.

## What This Package Does Not Own

It does not start Telegram, WhatsApp, or A2A transports, discover remote agents, persist memory, record run artifacts, or decide which collaborator to ask. It only exposes host-provided collaborators as a bounded MCP tool for a runtime to call.
